selection_rationale: autocand-2026-01 (Generate–Verify–Repair pipeline) best balances direct operational relevance to NetOps safety, methodological clarity and falsifiability, and feasibility within the provided compute/model-call budget. It directly targets verifier-grounded semantic error reduction (aligned with prior work e.g., W7157506260, doi:10.31224/7995) while remaining experimentally tractable for a five-page CNSM short paper.
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier false negatives and coverage (how often the verifier misses semantic violations).
Fidelity gap between the synthetic multi-vendor corpus and real vendor runtime/control-plane semantics.
Risk that LLM repair iterations introduce new, undetected semantic errors (hallucinations) not caught by the verifier.
Scope and scale of ground-truth labeling and emulator-verified validation (manual labeling limits coverage).
Degree to which verifier-detected violations correlate with real outage/operational harm in production environments.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Demonstrate verifier coverage and estimate false-negative rate on a stratified emulator-verified subset (or oracle) before claiming semantic-error reduction.
Include emulated/device-accurate execution (or justify and document digital-twin fidelity) for a stratified subset of vendor/task cases to validate verifier effectiveness.
Specify and pre-register power analysis, concrete sample-size targets, and explicit thresholds (e.g., >30% reduction) used for primary outcome claims.
Publish and freeze vendor templates, parsing/adaptation pipeline, and tests for vendor-syntax corner cases to ensure reproducibility and to minimize adapter-induced bias.
